subject: Service suppression — appeal for credit, evidence bundle request, and postmortem invite
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@brightserve.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+incidents@brightserve.com
Date: Sat, 7 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden suppression of generate responses — urgent confirmation + ask

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing a suppression in responses from the Redwood inference endpoint for our checkout-service at ~08:48 PDT this morning. Calls are returning 200 with empty or truncated bodies for many tokens and some requests are completing with 502s. This affected ~8% of user-facing transactions between 08:48–09:05.

Can you confirm whether this window qualifies as a downtime/service-suppression event under our SLA? Our billing team will need an initial confirmation to open an internal credit request. Also attaching a small trace bundle and the client-side capture.

Attachments: brightserve_request.pdf, client_capture.tar.gz (sent separately)

Thanks — Marco
Marco Ruiz
Senior SRE, BrightServe
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@brightserve.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Sep 2029 09:37:14 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden suppression of generate responses — urgent confirmation + ask

Hi Marco — thanks for the report and for attaching the bundle. We're pulling traces now. A few quick notes:

- We see a routing suppression event flagged by our edge layer at 08:47:53 PDT; some requests fell back to a lower-capacity variant which produced truncated outputs.
- I can't confirm eligibility for a credit just yet; policy requires correlation to a service-level "unavailable" window (5xx rate above threshold) and evidence of customer impact.

Laura / Vivek — please triage the traces attached and pull the server-side logs for the 08:40–09:10 window. Priorities: confirm exact window where 5xx rate crossed the SLA threshold, gather per-region request counts, and identify whether a routing policy or autoscaler preemption contributed.

Marco — we'll keep you updated and will request a formal log bundle and any client-side correlation timestamps you have. If eligible, we will follow the compensation workflow and schedule a postmortem.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account & Escalations Manager, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@brightserve.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Sep 2029 13:02:01 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden suppression of generate responses — urgent confirmation + ask

Hannah / Vivek — triage notes (quick summary; full log bundle attached in Drive link):

- Observed elevated 502/empty-body responses for BrightServe tenant in us-west-2 between 08:47:52–09:03:27 PDT. 5xx rate peak: 9.1% for a 3-minute contiguous window (08:48:10–08:51:09).
- Root cause preliminary: routing-layer backoff combined with a transient autoscaler oscillation on the dedicated pool handling BrightServe traffic. Several request batches were routed to a quantized variant with strict token cutoffs, causing truncated bodies in ~6% of requests.
- No indication of malicious traffic; CPU/GPU metrics do not show sustained saturation—it's an interaction between routing policy and pod churn.

Actions taken: collected host-level logs, KV cache traces, and the edge access logs. I've uploaded svc_traces-20290907.zip and slo-window-20290907.png to the Drive folder (link above).

Recommendation on entitlement: the observed 5xx peak and user-impacted request rate appear to meet the "service unavailable" criteria for the affected window. Recommend we offer a proportional credit for the 08:48–08:51 window and follow-up with a postmortem.

I'll be available for a short postmortem sync Monday; Hannah, can you propose a time to include BrightServe engineering?

Laura Bennett
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@brightserve.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, ops+incidents@brightserve.com
Date: Sun, 8 Sep 2029 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden suppression of generate responses — urgent confirmation + ask

Marco — thanks for patience. Per our internal review (summary below) we can confirm an eligible service-suppression window and propose a proportional credit:

What we found:
- Eligible window: 2029-09-07T08:48:10Z to 2029-09-07T08:51:09Z (three-minute contiguous interval where 5xx > SLA threshold).
- Impact: ~8% of BrightServe production requests returned truncated bodies or 502s; customer-observed errors align with our traces.
- Cause: routing backoff triggering fallback to a quantized variant during autoscaler churn.

Next steps / asks from BrightServe:
1) Please confirm the attached client-side timestamp mapping (brightserve_request.pdf) matches your internally-observed incidents so we can lock the exact billing window.
2) If you want the full raw log bundle delivered for compliance/billing, confirm and we will share a secured Drive ZIP (svc_traces-20290907.zip already in Drive).
3) Postmortem: suggest Monday 2029-09-09 10:00 AM PDT for a 45-minute call (invite will be sent after you confirm).

If you confirm the mapping, we'll initiate the compensation flow and provide the proposed pro-rata credit within 2 business days. Vivek and Laura will own the RCA and the remediation plan.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Account & Escalations Manager, Redwood Inference
